method: Lane model (agent2/night/scratch/A035/lanes.mjs): B and captured zombies all step 2C00h on the 400h lattice (in-page 52h). A zombie at speed 2 with trail 1048h has B's period (512+18 turns per B generation = (1042+18)/2 rounds), so it moves in exact 1:1 lockstep with B; offset to B = (phase - 1000h) - n*2C00h with generation lag n in {0,1} at start (zombie gen0 is shorter). Lethal offsets (B trail covers zombie anchor, merge, or zombie trail covers B anchor) are slots {-4..+1} of 400h; zombie-zombie lethal |d|<=4. Exact 2:1 lockstep (rev0 trail 800h) would need step 1600h/9600h, i.e. odd generations off the 400h lattice, so it was not built. Implementation without changing B's main path: phoenix_init mov dx,02400h -> lea dx,[bp+2400h] (main path BP=0 at entry, so DX=2400h as rev0); the zombie tail sets BP=0F7B8h -> DX=1BB8h (trail 1048h). Death attribution helper agent2/night/scratch/A035/ana.mjs (writer of the byte at the fatal IP; captured zombies = zom20* with CS=0FFBh).

threatFindings.threat: Captured zombies on drifting lanes (rev0: speed 2, same step as B, about one generation gained per B generation) cross B: zombie trails kill B and B/A trails kill the zombies
threatFindings.evidence: Base trace pkj3o (nightTR-6861894f3c-8579e2c221, 168 battles): B deaths with the fatal byte written by a zombie 6 (zom20b 5), captured zombies killed by A/B bytes 13. Lane-locked LK trace xx1xi: 2 and 2; LKbd trace nja6y: B 2.
threatFindings.impact: Small: at most about 6 B deaths per 168 battles plus some zombie lifetime. The screens show no score gain from removing it (k19kd -0.010, mwoox -0.0085).

threatFindings.threat: 1:1 lockstep on a lane chosen from the lag model separates captured zombies from B
threatFindings.evidence: Traces xx1xi (LK) and nja6y (LKbd) show the predicted removal of B<-zombie and (LK) zombie<-partner kills. The model also explains A013's z1000 loss: with z1000's phases, the b/d lane offset at lag 1 is -800h (zombie trail over B's anchor, lethal) and the zom20a lane is safe; trace 46uvt has 53 B deaths by zom20b/d and none by zom20a.
threatFindings.impact: The mechanism works but is worth less than the noise of a screen; it does not improve the score.

threatFindings.threat: Locking zom20a in step with B raises A's deaths by zombie-written bytes
threatFindings.evidence: LK trace xx1xi: A<-zombie 10 (zom20a 8) vs base 3 and LKbd 3 (zom20a not locked). Counts are small (Poisson p about 0.05). Uniform-mixing argument (a zombie writes 8 bytes/round whatever its step) predicts no change.
threatFindings.impact: May cancel the B-side gain in LK.

threatFindings.threat: Exact 2:1 lockstep of speed-2 zombies with B (rev0 trail 800h) is possible on the lattice
threatFindings.evidence: Static arithmetic: 2S = 2C00h mod 10000h gives S = 1600h or 9600h, so every odd generation is 200h off the 400h lattice. On-lattice lockstep needs a 1:1 ratio (trail 1048h).
threatFindings.impact: Rules out the cheapest lane-lock design.

threatFindings.threat: GSA_callfart cohort is sensitive to any change of the zombie trail/step (A013: -0.239 in all three variants)
threatFindings.evidence: LK changes the trail/step of both zombie paths without moving zombie_entry: zomb_callfart 0 (k19kd); LKbd +0.022 (mwoox).
threatFindings.impact: A013's constant callfart loss was more likely caused by its layout or FAR_SEG-register change than by the zombie parameters.

recommendation: Do not promote either candidate. Lane-locking the captured zombies to B works as designed (traces: B deaths by zombie-written bytes 6 -> 2, zombies killed by our bytes 13 -> 2 in LK), but both screens are slightly negative on ALL (-0.010, -0.0085) and on the 2025 group (-0.030, -0.020), and LKbd's multi group is negative in both cohorts. The rev0 zombie speed already sits between B's and A's, so it crosses its partners about as little as possible overall; the only thing lane separation can remove is the B-zombie share, which is about 6 B deaths per 168 battles. Card closed. If anyone revisits it, the on-lattice 1:1 lock (trail 1048h) and the lag model in lanes.mjs are the tools to use; avoid phases where any lag in -2..+3 gives an offset of -1000h..+400h from B's anchor.
